My true preference is w > x > y > z. However, I need to consider the priorities and the preferences of other students to maximize my chances of getting a good match.

Most applicants favor y > x > w > z. This means y is likely to be very competitive. I have top priority at both w and y. Since my true preference is w > y, I want to secure w if possible.

If I rank w first, I will be tentatively accepted in the first round. The only way I would be rejected from w is if a student with higher priority than me proposes. Since I have priority 1 at w, this is impossible. Thus, ranking w first guarantees me w.

Therefore, the optimal strategy is to rank w first to secure my top choice. The rest of my ranking can follow my true preferences.

If I don't get x, I want w. If I rank w second, I might get it. However, many students prefer y > x > w > z. This means that w might be oversubscribed with students who rank y first but get rejected. Since my priority at w is 2, I might get rejected from w as well.

If I rank y second, I might get it. However, since my true preference is w > y, I'd rather get w.

If I rank z second, I am guaranteed to get z if x and w reject me. But since my priority at z is 1, it's likely that z will be available even if I rank it last.

Therefore, I should rank x first, w second, y third, and z last. This is because I have the highest priority at x, so I should rank it first. If I don't get x, I want w, so I rank it second. Then y, then z, according to my preferences.

If I put z before y, I might get matched to z, which is even worse.

Therefore, submitting my true preferences should give me the best outcome.
